$comment: Types that hold an IStepDispatcher and are NOT decorators of it.
EveryDispatcherDecoratorForwardsEveryMember finds a decorator structurally: a type that
implements IStepDispatcher and holds one. That predicate is deliberately wide, because the
two defects PLAN section 9 item 12 records were both hand-written harnesses holding the
GENERATED dispatcher by its concrete type -- a shape a narrower predicate missed entirely.
Wide catches three things that are not decorators, and the difference is what a held
a decorator holds the inner one because its whole contract is 'that, plus something'.
Every member it does not forward is a feature it silently switches off.
a sub-flow composer holds a CHILD's dispatcher, for one step. Its own journal entries,
cache keys and audit records are its own; answering for itself is correct, and forwarding
would attribute the parent's steps to the child.
a stub holds one it never dispatches to, because a constructor took it.
A row here is a claim of the second or third kind, and it must say which. The list can only
shrink: a type that starts forwarding is reported, so an entry cannot outlive its reason.

notDecorators.why: Generated. It holds the child flow's dispatcher for the SubFlow step and nothing else; its DescribeStep, cache keys and audit records describe the parent's own steps. Forwarding them would file the parent's journal under the child.
The double for the shape above, holding a child plan and its dispatcher for one step. Same reason, and it exists to measure the engine's allocations rather than to add behaviour to anything.
Takes a child in its constructor and never calls it: every member answers Success so a drain can be observed without a flow doing work. There is nothing to forward to.
